title: Kyokushinkai Sanbon Kumite
author: isshin dojo一心
description:
Although kyokushin karate has evolved into a combat sport with a lot of emphasis on it's competition based training pre-arranged kumite form-training is still of vital importance for true Budo development. Ippon Kumite (one step), Sanbon Kumite (three step) are part of so called Yakusoku Kumite and basically Karate's essentials. Just like kata they require speed, technique, form, focus, timing, precise execution and impact.  Let's hold them dear! Osu

author: isshin dojo一心

Kazumi's 100-Men Kumite took place in 1995. Kazumi is one of the strongest tournament fighters ever to occur. With an almost elusive like but very grounded style that included devastating lowkicks as well as the philosophy of internal body mechanics he defeated many opponents.

title: Dutch Open Kyokushinkai Championships 1990 (Zutphen, The Netherlands)
author: isshin dojo一心
description:
I stumbled upon this version of the offical tournament footage made by Nikko Toshogu Press back in the day. This one has splendid colours and is lacking the English narrative which was added for the UK-market in another version. Wow, what a treat! There was so much quality involved back then. All fighters more or less belonged to one big organisation. Great kumite and great sportmanship. 

(Much thanks obliged to the original uploader. Domo arigato 🙏🏼)

title: Kyokushinkaikan | World Tournament IKO 1979
author: isshin dojo一心
description:
The 2nd Kyokushin Karate Open World Championships at the Japan Metropolitan Gymnasium in 1979. Vintage like noble wine. Very nice footage, great to watch. 

Among the participants back then are many household names in the international world of full contact karate today. Shihan like for instance B. Creton, H. Collins, K. Scharrenberg, M. Nakamura, K. Sanpei and all others were setting the pace back then. Paving the way for future generations. Also among them the later famously known 'universal soldier' D. Lundgren from Sweden. Grass roots kyokushin.
